text.fit: Calibrated on 2023-07-30 (wind 030 deg) and 2024-07-16 (wind 190 deg) - opposite wind directions, so a real downwind plume signal would switch sides between the two scenes. Held-out validation on 2024-08-25 (wind 210 deg).
text.skill: calibration R2 0.86 / 0.84, RMSE 1.58 / 1.52 K; held-out R2 0.81, RMSE 1.36 K (model without the data-center terms: R2 0.80, RMSE 1.41 K)
text.plume_term: gamma*F/F0 = -0.015 (90% bootstrap interval -0.34 to 0.28): the simulated downwind near-ground warming is NOT detected in Landsat LST.
text.heat_flux: With the prior gamma ~ N(0.6, 0.15) the effective (sensible, near-surface-coupled) heat-rejection flux of existing campuses is F = -30 W/m2 of roof (median), 90% interval -493 to 383 W/m2, i.e. consistent with zero and below ~383 W/m2 at 95% confidence.
text.physics_check: A 100 MW-IT campus with PUE 1.3 rejects ~130 MW; on 15-25 ha of roof that is 520-870 W/m2 if all heat left as sensible heat at roof level (the new-campus design value here: 120 MW / 14.8 ha = 810 W/m2). The satellite upper bound (~383 W/m2, i.e. <= 712 MW over the 186 ha of operational data-center roofs in the AOI) is below that, which is consistent with a large share of heat leaving as latent heat (evaporative/adiabatic cooling) and/or exhaust plumes rising above the near-surface layer - or with the prototype's plumes being too narrow/too low so the signal is mis-placed. LST alone cannot separate these.
text.roof_term: g_roof = -5.76 K (90% -7.88 to -3.94) per unit data-center roof fraction after roof-darkness terms: data-center roofs read cooler than comparable large roofs (reflective membranes, rooftop equipment shading/evaporation), so the rooftop term cannot be read as heat rejection (delta*F is negative, not physical).
text.used_in_scenarios: Existing campuses in the scenario runs reject 400 W/m2 of roof (~743 MW in the AOI), a round value at the satellite-consistent 90% upper bound (383-466 W/m2 depending on bootstrap replicate count); the new campus uses the design 120 MW (810 W/m2), i.e. an upper-bound, all-sensible case. Near-surface warming scales roughly linearly with flux, so a campus behaving like the satellite-calibrated median would produce much smaller warming.

solver.type: 3-D lattice Boltzmann (D3Q19) for the urban boundary-layer flow + D3Q7 lattice Boltzmann advection-diffusion for the potential-temperature anomaly, fused GPU kernel (numba.cuda, RTX 4090)
solver.collision: regularized BGK with Smagorinsky LES eddy viscosity (Cs=0.16) plus a non-local K-profile eddy viscosity/diffusivity for the daytime convective boundary layer (Holtslag-Boville form, K = kappa w_m z (1-z/h)^2), turbulent Prandtl 0.7
solver.forcing: Guo forcing: Boussinesq buoyancy g*theta/T0 (T0 = 303 K); log-law surface drag (wall model) in the first fluid layer above terrain with z0 from WorldCover (tree 1.0 m, built 0.5 m, grass 0.03 m, crop 0.05 m, water 0.0002 m)
solver.geometry: terrain (3DEP) and buildings (footprints + heights) as solid cells, half-way bounce-back (no-slip, adiabatic); 600 x 600 x 64 cells at 10 m (6 x 6 x 0.64 km), 23.0 M cells
solver.boundaries: inflow faces: equilibrium with measured-wind power-law profile (U10 from KIAD, alpha 0.14, constant above 150 m); outflow faces: non-equilibrium extrapolation with density pinned to 1 plus a 160 m viscous sponge; lid: free slip with a 120 m absorbing sponge (stands in for the deeper boundary layer)
solver.heat_sources: rooftop heat rejection injected into the first fluid cell above each data-center roof cell, proportional to roof area (W per m2 of roof)
solver.time_step: dt = 0.1 dx / U_max (0.12-0.27 s depending on the day), Mach < 0.2
solver.performance_mlups: ~920-990 million lattice updates per second; one 40-minute simulated period takes ~4-7 min wall time
solver.near_surface_definition: "2 m" values are taken from the first fluid cell above the surface (terrain or roof), i.e. the 0-10 m layer, centre ~5 m above ground
